topics.topic: Your phone weakens your thinking even when you are not using it

items.claim: Just having your phone nearby makes your brain use less energy for thinking tasks.
items.quote: Results from two experiments indicate that even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

items.claim: Phone presence hurts working memory, but does not stop you from paying attention.
items.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

items.claim: Having a phone visible makes people do worse on attention tests.
items.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

items.claim: People who depend on phones the most lose the most thinking power when the phone is there.
items.quote: Moreover, these cognitive costs are highest for those highest in smartphone dependence.

items.claim: A huge study of thousands of people found phone presence does not change thinking skills.
items.quote: It was found that the mere presence of smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes (d = −0.02, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.01], p = .246).

claims.verdict: Evidence is split between studies showing phone presence reduces working memory and attention, and a large meta-analysis finding no significant effect on cognitive outcomes.
claims.caveat: The field shows substantial methodological heterogeneity and generally poor statistical power.

json.title: The Phone That Eats Your Mind

hooks.text: Your phone is stealing your power.
You think you are focused. The data says you are not.
Do you check your phone while you try to remember something?
An empty room with a phone on the table.

reveal.headline: A visible phone reduces energy for thinking.
reveal.body: Just having the device nearby drains cognitive power, even if you do not touch it.

explain.headline: Your brain treats the phone as a threat.
explain.body: When the phone is visible, your brain stays on guard. This guard takes energy from working memory.

matters.headline: You cannot simply turn it off.
matters.body: Dependence makes the loss worse. You lose thinking power in moments you do not control.

example.headline: The dinner table.
example.body: You sit to read a book. The phone sits across the table. You cannot finish the sentence you started.

question.headline: Where does your phone sit right now?
question.body: Think of the answer before you read this caption.

json.caption: Your phone weakens your thinking even when it is silent and still. This is not a myth. It is a measurable cost of the device being nearby.
